items.s:
With reference to the use of nanotechnology in health sector, which of the following statements is/are correct?

a. Targeted drug delivery is made possible by nanotechnology

b. Nanotechnology can largely contribute to gene therapy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
items.x: Nanoparticles enable targeted drug delivery, and nanoparticle carriers help deliver genes in gene therapy, so both are correct (UPSC 2015 key c).

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: Which of the following factors will NOT generally cause heart disease?
o: Deficiency of Vitamin A in diet
items.x: High blood pressure, high blood glucose and raised lipids are risk factors for heart disease; vitamin A deficiency is not, so it is the answer.

items.s: The plant dye henna imparts orange-red colour to skin and hairs due to its reaction with which of the following?
items.x: Lawsone, the dye of henna, binds to the proteins (keratin) and amino acids of skin and hair, giving the orange-red stain. It does not react with lipids, carbohydrates or nucleic acids.

items.s: Solar energy is drawn from which of the following :
items.x: Solar energy is the radiant energy of the Sun.

items.s: 'Audio conferencing' is
items.x: Audio conferencing is a live voice call among two or more parties, so it is two-sided verbal communication; there are no visual or non-verbal cues. Off-topic here; moved to ICT in day-to-day life.

items.s: To move to the bottom of a document, press
items.x: Ctrl + End moves to the bottom (end) of the document; the End key alone only moves to the end of the current line. Off-topic, moved to software.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
Match each strategy for sustainable development with its corresponding example of implementation.
Strategies:
A. Renewable Energy
B. Sustainable Agriculture
C. Waste Reduction
Implementation:
1. Crop Rotation
2. Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
3. Solar Power
items.x: Renewable energy – solar power; sustainable agriculture – crop rotation; waste reduction – reduce, reuse, recycle: A-3, B-1, C-2.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
items.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

items.s: The Plant Field Gene Bank at Banthara will :
items.x: NBRI's field gene bank at Banthara (Lucknow) preserves endangered plants, identifies economically useful wild plants and helps check biopiracy, so all of the above.

items.s: A form of virus explicitly designed to hide itself from detection by antivirus software is called as
items.x: A stealth virus hides itself from antivirus detection; a boot-sector virus infects the boot record and a metamorphic virus rewrites its code.

items.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
items.s: Proline is a type of _______.
items.x: Proline is one of the 20 amino acids that make up proteins (a non-essential one). It is not a base, a bacterium or a virus.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Hard coffee stains on clothes can be properly removed by?
items.x: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is an oxidising agent that breaks down the coloured compounds of tea and coffee stains on white cloth. Water and lemon juice only lighten fresh stains, and petrol removes grease, not coffee.

items.s: The first mechanical computer was fabricated in 1642 by
items.x: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline, the first mechanical calculating machine, in 1642; Babbage's engines came in the 19th century.

items.s: Which company, in collaboration with ISRO, launched the "High-throughput satellite (HTS)" broadband internet service?
items.x: Hughes Communications India launched India's first high-throughput satellite (HTS) broadband service in 2022, using capacity on ISRO's GSAT-11 and GSAT-29.

items.s: All the slides of MS PowerPoint presentation can be viewed in a single screen by using __.
items.x: Slide Sorter view shows all slides as thumbnails on one screen; Slide Show runs them one at a time and Master view edits the template. (Computers; moved to row 12.)

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Which of the following statements is not valid about operator overloading?
o: Only existing operators can be overloaded
Overloaded operator must have at least one operand of its class type
The overloaded operators follow the syntax rules of the original operator
items.x: All three statements are true rules of C++ operator overloading (only existing operators, at least one class-type operand, original syntax kept), so 'None of the above' is the answer.

items.s: Which one of the following statements about air pollution caused by diesel engines is correct?
o: It produces large quantity of carbon monoxide at lower and high temperatures.
It produces large quantity of nitrogen oxides at lower and high temperatures.
It produces large quantity of carbon monoxide at lower temperature and nitrogen oxides at high temperature.
It produces large quantity of nitrogen oxides at lower temperature and carbon monoxide at high temperature.
items.x: Diesel engines give much CO at low temperature (incomplete combustion) and much NOx at high temperature (nitrogen and oxygen combine in the hot cylinder).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
items.s: A study preceeding the main study to check the viability is known as:
items.x: A pilot study is a small preliminary study run before the main study to test its feasibility and tools.

items.s: Who was the first commercial Mobile service provider in India?
items.x: India's first commercial mobile service was Modi Telstra's MobileNet in Kolkata: the first call on 31 July 1995 (Jyoti Basu to Sukh Ram); BSNL's CellOne came only in 2002.

items.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Dark Reserve is a public or private land with a distinguished nocturnal environment and starry nights that has been developed responsibly to prevent light pollution.

II. World's 1st International Dark Sky Reserve is Mont-Megantic, located in Russia.

III. The International Dark-Sky Association (IDSA) is a US-based non-profit organisation that designates sites as international dark sky places.

IV. The Department of Science & Technology (DST) has announced the setting up of India's 1st Dark-Sky Reserve in Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.x: Statement I (definition) and III (the US-based IDA, now DarkSky International, certifies sites) are correct. II is wrong (Mont-Mégantic is in Canada) and IV is wrong (India's first reserve is Hanle, Ladakh). No option offers 'I and III only', so 'None of the above' is the key.

items.src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
items.s: According to recent study of IIT, Mumbai what is the approximate cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015?
items.x: An IIT Bombay study put the economic cost of air pollution in Delhi and Mumbai in 2015 at about Rs 70,000 crore. Pollution item, moved.

items.s: The Indian Institute of Ecology and Environment is located at–
items.x: The Indian Institute of Ecology and Environment is in New Delhi; Mumbai, Kolkata and Thiruvananthapuram are distractors.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
items.x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

items.s: Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) is located at:
items.x: The Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR) is at Kochi (Cochin), Kerala.

items.s: What is Dakshin Gangotri?
o: Second sources of River Ganga in the South of Gangotri
Island in the Indian Ocean near Antarctica
items.x: Dakshin Gangotri was India's first Antarctic research station, set up in 1983-84. It is not a river valley, a source of the Ganga or an island.

items.s:
While India’s Human population is growing at an astounding pace, the bird population is shrinking fastly mainly because

I. there has been an abnormal increase in the number of hunters.

II. bio-pesticides and organic manure are being used on an large scale.

III. there has been a large scale reduction in the habitats of birds.

IV. there has been a large scale use of pesticides, chemical fertilisers and mosquito repellents.
Select your answer correctly using the codes given below.
items.x: Birds are declining mainly through habitat reduction (III) and heavy use of pesticides, chemical fertilisers and mosquito repellents (IV). Bio-pesticides and organic manure are harmless, and hunting is not the main cause.

items.s:
Scientist led by PRL Professor discovered new Jupiter size exoplanet in May 2023.
Which of the following statements is/are correct in this context?

I. The mass of this exoplanet is 13 times that of Jupiter.

II. The team was led by professor Abhijit Chakraborty at the exoplanet research group of the physical research laboratory.
items.x: Both are correct: the exoplanet TOI-4603b found by PRL (May 2023) is about 13 times Jupiter's mass, and the team was led by Prof. Abhijit Chakraborty of PRL's exoplanet group.

items.s: Which life form consists of a single nucleic acid, of either DNA or RNA?
items.x: A virus contains only one kind of nucleic acid, either DNA or RNA. Amoeba, bacteria and plant cells have both.

items.s: In which place the first Indian Defence Industrial Park is proposed?
items.x: India's first Defence Industrial Park was set up by KINFRA at Ottapalam (Palakkad), Kerala.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
items.s: Which Indian scientist has developed 'Cytotron' device. The device has been designated as the breakthrough device by the Centre for Devices and Radiological Health, a branch of the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) for treatment of liver, pancreatic and breast cancer treatment?
items.x: Dr Rajah Vijay Kumar (Scalene Cybernetics, Bengaluru) developed the Cytotron, given 'Breakthrough Device' status by the US FDA's CDRH.

items.s:
Which of the following are some important pollutants released by the steel industry in India?
1. Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxides of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
items.x: The steel industry releases oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, CO and CO2 – all four.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
items.s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of mass communication?
items.x: Mass communication is impersonal, reaches a large and scattered audience and passes through gatekeepers, but its feedback is delayed and indirect, so instant feedback is not one of its characteristics. Off-topic here; moved to media.

items.s:
Consider the following in view of PSLV-C53 :

A. It was launched from the second launch pad of Satish Dhawan Space Centre on June 30, 2022.

B. It is the dedicated commercial mission of Antrix Corporation.

C. The launch vehicle carried three satellites from Singapore, namely DS-EO, NeuSAR, Scoob-1.
Choose the correct answer :
items.x: A and C are right: PSLV-C53 flew from the second launch pad on 30 June 2022 carrying Singapore's DS-EO, NeuSAR and SCOOB-I. B is wrong: it was NSIL's (not Antrix's) second dedicated commercial mission.

items.s: Climate change is caused by
items.x: Commonly keyed 'all of the above': GHGs are the main cause; ozone depletion and pollution (aerosols, black carbon) also alter climate.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: For how many years was the Endangered Species Recovery Plan for an initial level started under the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Advisory Council?
items.x: The Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species, funded through the National CAMPA Advisory Council, was sanctioned for an initial 5 years.

items.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.
2. Gasohol is a mixture of benzene and alcohol.
3. Geothermal energy is non-conventional energy source.
4. Gobar gas contains mainly methane. Of these statements :
items.x: Coal, petroleum and gas are fossil fuels, geothermal is non-conventional, and gobar gas is mainly methane. Statement 2 is wrong: gasohol is petrol (gasoline) plus alcohol, not benzene plus alcohol. So 1, 3 and 4.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
items.x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following is the heaviest satellite vehicle India has ever launched?
items.x:
GSAT-19 was the record in 2017 — now CMS-03 (GSAT-7R, 4,410 kg, LVM3-M5, Nov 2025) is the heaviest communication satellite launched from India, and BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg) the heaviest payload (app notes 5:35 sub 7, 5:37 sub 2)
When this was set, GSAT-19 (3,136 kg, GSLV Mk III-D1, Jun 2017) was the heaviest satellite India had launched itself; GSAT-16 and GSAT-18 were heavier but went up on Ariane, and GSAT-21 does not exist (now CMS-03, 4,410 kg, is the heaviest comsat from Indian soil).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Who was the first woman to go to space?
items.x: Valentina Tereshkova (USSR, Vostok-6, 1963) was the first woman in space.

items.s:
Read the following pairs :

a. 12th biennial edition of 'International Aerospace and Defence Exhibition' was inaugurated by : The Defence Minister (Raksha Mantri) of India

b. The iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) scheme was launched by : The Prime Minister of India
Choose the correct answer :
o: Both a and b are not correct
Both a and b are correct
items.x: Both pairs are correct: the 12th Aero India (Feb 2019, Bengaluru) was inaugurated by the Defence Minister, and iDEX was launched by the Prime Minister in April 2018.

items.s: Which of the following is not a major IT Company in India?
items.x: Raymond is a textile and apparel company; CMC (now part of TCS), Infosys and TCS are IT companies.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Where was India's first waste-to-energy plant established?
items.x: India's first waste-to-energy plant was set up at Timarpur, Delhi, in 1987.

items.s: Which of the following noble gases is NOT present in the air?
items.x:
Most books: all noble gases except radon occur in air. Strictly, radon is present in trace amounts near the ground (decay of radium in soil).
Argon, neon and helium are constituents of air. Radon is radioactive and short-lived, so it is taken as the noble gas not present in air. (Off-topic: chemistry.)

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Honey is sweeter than cane sugar or corn syrup. Which one of the following carbon sugars is responsible for this?
items.x:
Levulose (option 2) is the same sugar as fructose, so both options are chemically right; keyed 'Fructose' as the standard name.
Honey is sweeter than cane sugar mainly because of fructose, the sweetest sugar. Levulose is only another name for fructose; dextrose (glucose) and sucrose are less sweet.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: Respiration is an
items.x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

items.s: A function inside another function in excel is called
items.x: A function used inside another function in Excel is a nested function, e.g. =ROUND(SUM(A1:A5),0). Round and Sum are single functions.

items.s: Which one of the following device is non-Ohmic?
items.x: A semiconductor diode is non-ohmic: its current-voltage graph is non-linear and it conducts in one direction. Copper coils, heating coils and rheostats obey Ohm's law.

items.s: As per Indian State of Forest Report (ISFR)-2015, what is the total carbon stock in forests of India?
items.x: ISFR 2015 put the carbon stock of India's forests at 7,044 million tonnes. (Moved to 5:104.)

items.s: The largest Telecom operator in India is
items.x:
BSNL was the largest operator in 2003 — now Reliance Jio is the largest by subscribers (general knowledge, TRAI data)
In 2003 BSNL was India's largest telecom operator.

items.s: The theme of the World Environment Day 2022 was ______.
items.x: World Environment Day 2022 (hosted by Sweden, 50 years after Stockholm) had the theme 'Only One Earth'; 'Beat Plastic Pollution' was 2018/2023 and 'Invest in Our Planet' an Earth Day theme.

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
items.s: Which of the following awards of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, were announced for the first time during ANGAN 2022?
o: National Energy Efficiency Roadmap for Movement towards Affordable and Natural Habitat Awards
The Special Meritorious Awards for Engineering Innovation
The Spotlight on New Technology Small Business Awards
items.x: At ANGAN 2022, BEE announced the NEERMAN Awards (National Energy Efficiency Roadmap for Movement towards Affordable & Natural Habitat) for the first time. They honour energy-efficient building design.

items.s:
Regarding Agni-III which is/are correct?

a. It is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile

b. Its range is 3,500 kms

c. While the first flight of Agni-III in 2006 failed, its second and third flights in 2007 and 2008 were successful.
items.x: Agni-III is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile of about 3,500 km range; its first flight (9 July 2006) failed and the second (April 2007) and third (May 2008) succeeded. So all three statements are correct.

items.s:
Consider the following statements :

A. In November, 2006, DRDO successfully conducted the interception test using Prithvi II missile.

B. Prithvi-II is a surface-to-surface missile and can be deployed to guard the metros against air attacks.
Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
items.x: On 27 November 2006 DRDO's PAD interceptor (a modified Prithvi) destroyed a Prithvi-II target – the interception test of statement A. Prithvi-II is an offensive surface-to-surface missile, not a weapon to guard metros against air attack, so B is wrong.

items.s: In fibre optic communication the source of Light used is:
items.x:
LEDs are also used as sources for short multimode links; the usual key is the semiconductor laser.
Long-distance optical fibre links use semiconductor lasers (laser diodes), which give narrow, coherent, high-speed light. LEDs serve only short, low-speed links, and a CFL is never used.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: What are the names of the two ships which collided in January, 2017 near Chennai causing oil spill?
items.x: On 28 January 2017 the LPG tanker BW Maple and the oil tanker MT Dawn Kanchipuram collided off Kamarajar (Ennore) port near Chennai, causing an oil spill.

items.s: In which year did the first Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) of India commence in Andhra Pradesh to cater to the needs of smallscale industries?
items.x: India's first Common Effluent Treatment Plant for small-scale industry clusters began at Jeedimetla near Hyderabad (then Andhra Pradesh) in 1989.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: The data related to food items issued to students is received on the same day at Head Office in the institutions run by APSWREIS by using?
items.x: Printed key: the ANNAPURNA app, used in APSWREIS institutions so that data on food items issued to students reaches the head office the same day. (AP welfare / e-governance item, moved.)

items.src: APPSC Assistant Section Officer (ASO) Mains General Studies
items.s: Recently, Supreme Court banned the use of following substances in firecrackers?
items.x: The Supreme Court (2017–18) banned heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic, antimony and lithium, plus barium salts, in firecrackers. Sulphur and potassium nitrate are still standard cracker ingredients.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
items.s: Which of the following symptom is not associated with gastro intestinal disease?
items.x: GI diseases cause diarrhoea, vomiting, nausea and abdominal pain; kidney failure is not a GI symptom.

items.s: As per Sustainable Development Goals India Index-Baseline Report-2018, for the construction of SDG India Index, NITI Aayog left out which one of the following SDG?
items.x: The 2018 Baseline SDG India Index scored only 13 goals (39 targets, 62 indicators); SDG 12 (Sustainable Consumption and Production), 13, 14 and 17 were left out, while Education, Gender Equality and Clean Energy were included.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Fasciolosis in cattle causes which type of jaundice
items.x: Liver flukes block the bile ducts, so fasciolosis causes obstructive (post-hepatic) jaundice.

items.s:
Which of the following practices can help in water conservation in agriculture?

I. Reduced or zero tillage of the land.

II. Applying gypsum before irrigating the field.

III. Allowing crop residue to remain in the field.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
items.x: Reduced or zero tillage and leaving crop residue on the field conserve soil moisture; gypsum is a soil amendment for sodicity, not a water-saving step, so 1 and 3 (UPSC 2017).

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: Which of the following seeds have wings that help in seed dispersal?
items.x: Drumstick (Moringa) and maple seeds are winged and dispersed by wind; Xanthium and Urena have hooks, castor and balsam burst open.

items.s:
Choose the correct option based on the statements below:
Statement I: Biodegradable plastics are a better alternative to traditional plastics
Statement II: The production of some biodegradable plastics requires large amounts of energy and resources, and their disposal can still contribute to environmental pollution.
items.x: Both statements are true. Biodegradable plastics are a better alternative to conventional plastics, but some need much energy and resources to make and can still pollute on disposal.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Borrow pit is ____
items.at: a pit from which construction material is taken for use
items.x: A borrow pit is a pit from which earth, sand or gravel is dug for use as fill elsewhere (roads, embankments).

items.s: The College of Military Engineering affiliated to Jawaharlal Nehru University is situated at
items.x: The College of Military Engineering (CME), the Army's engineering college, is at Dapodi, Pune, and is affiliated to JNU. It is not in New Delhi, Dehradun (IMA) or Nainital.

items.s: Who among the following is world’s first woman cosmonaut :
items.x: Valentina Tereshkova (USSR) was the first woman in space, on Vostok-6, 16 June 1963. Bachendri Pal and Junko Tabei are Everest climbers; Sally Ride was the first American woman in space.

items.s:
Consider the following:

a. Satellites move around the earth with the same speed as the Earth spins

b. Satellites cover every part of earth except poles and surrounding areas which are out of their range
o: Both a and b are true
Neither a nor b is true
items.x:
No printed key. If the stem means geostationary satellites only, both a and b would be true (option c).
Taken generally, neither holds: only geostationary satellites keep pace with the Earth's spin, and polar-orbiting satellites do cover the poles.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: E-PG Pathshala is hosted at
items.x:
printed answer 'INFLIBNET, Ahmedabad' — now INFLIBNET Centre, Infocity, Gandhinagar (general knowledge, not checked)
e-PG Pathshala (MoE/UGC portal of PG e-content) is hosted by the INFLIBNET Centre, which is now at Gandhinagar, Gujarat (formerly Ahmedabad).

items.s: Check these statements : (i) Brass is an alloy of Copper and Zinc. (ii) Magnetite is the main ore of Aluminium. (iii) Amalgams are that substances which mainly involve mercury. (iv) Potassium Nitrate (KNO3) is a chemical used in photography. Which of the above are true ? Code :
items.x: (i) Brass = copper + zinc and (iii) amalgams are mercury alloys are true. Magnetite (Fe3O4) is an iron ore, and photography uses silver bromide, not KNO3, so (i) and (iii).

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: SpaceEx is
o: a space craft launched from Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh
a space craft launched from NASA, USA
an aerospace manufacturer and space transport services company, USA
a rocket and space craft launching private company, Russia
items.x: SpaceX is a US aerospace manufacturer and space-transport company founded by Elon Musk (2002); it is not a spacecraft or a Russian firm.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
items.s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
items.x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

items.s:
Identify incorrect pair regarding ecology.

I. Tropical rain forests - Base of mountains

II. Niche - Special position of the food chain

III. Biomass - Living material that can be converted into energy

IV. Biological control - Predator of parasite of the crop
items.x:
No printed key. Elton defined the niche by an animal's place in the food chain, so pair II can be read as correct; key (a) I, II is the best fit.
Pair I is wrong: tropical rainforests grow in hot wet lowlands near the equator, not at the base of mountains. Pair II is taken as wrong because a niche is the whole functional role of a species, not just its place in a food chain; III and IV are right.

items.src: Civil Asst Surgeon, Group-IV, District Probation Officer, Fo
items.s: Which one of the following is the major challenge in achieving SDGs related to poverty eradication?
o: Lack of awareness about the SDGs
High levels of investment in social programs
Economic inequality and unequal distribution of resources
items.x: Economic inequality and unequal distribution of resources are the main barrier to ending poverty; oversupply of resources or high social investment are not challenges.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s:
Match the Nobel Prize winners - 2024 with their countries.
Name:
1. David Baker
2. Demis Hassabis
3. Han Kang
Country:
A. USA
B. United Kingdom
C. South Korea
items.x: 2024 laureates: David Baker – USA (Chemistry), Demis Hassabis – UK (Chemistry), Han Kang – South Korea (Literature).

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: What was the focal theme of the National Biodiversity Congress held February, 2017 at Kerala?
items.x: The National Biodiversity Congress (Thiruvananthapuram, Feb 2017) had the focal theme 'Mainstreaming Biodiversity for Sustainable Development'.

items.s:
Match the following:
Day - Date

a) National Science Day - i) October, 8

b) Air Force Day - ii) February, 28

c) Navy Day - iii) May, 21

d) Anti Terrorism day - iv) December, 4
items.x: Science Day 28 February (ii), Air Force Day 8 October (i), Navy Day 4 December (iv), Anti-Terrorism Day 21 May (iii).

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: Which type of concrete paint among the following is used for areas with high chemical exposure?
items.x: Epoxy coatings resist chemicals and are used on concrete floors with high chemical exposure; acrylic latex paints are not chemical-resistant.

items.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Children's Climate Change Risk Index'?

I. It was initiated by the World Health Organisation (WHO) in 2005.

II. It ranks countries based on children's exposure to climate and environmental shocks as well as their vulnerability to those shocks, based on their access to essential services.
items.x: The Children's Climate Risk Index was launched by UNICEF in 2021, not by WHO in 2005, so I is wrong. II correctly describes it: countries are ranked on children's exposure to shocks and their vulnerability from access to services.

items.s: The chief mosquito repellent is obtained from –
items.x: Neem (margosa) is the chief natural mosquito repellent; its leaves and seed oil repel insects.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s:
Match the following winners of the Nobel Prize in 2019 with the respective categories in which they won.
Category:
I. Nobel Prize in Physics
II. Nobel Prize in Chemistry
III. Nobel Prize in Literature
IV. Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
Winners:
1. John B Goodenough, M Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino
2. Peter Handke
3. William G Kaelin Jr, Sir Peter J Ratcliffe and Gregg L Semenza
4. James Peebles
items.x: 2019: Physics – James Peebles (4); Chemistry – Goodenough, Whittingham, Yoshino (1); Literature – Peter Handke (2); Medicine – Kaelin, Ratcliffe, Semenza (3).

items.s: What is the approximate weight of the rocket GSLV Mark III D1?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (About 640 tonnes); it is added as option 5.
GSLV Mk III-D1 weighed about 640 t at lift-off, so none of the printed tonnage options is right. 3-4.5 t is payload scale: its GSAT-19 weighed 3,136 kg, and LVM3 lifts about 4 t to GTO.

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
items.s: Through Union Budget 2022-23, the Government of India allocated about ____ crore to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
items.x: Budget 2022-23 gave the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare about Rs 86,200 crore.

items.s: College of Defence Management is located at
items.x: The College of Defence Management is at Secunderabad; Wellington has the Defence Services Staff College and Dehradun the IMA.

items.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
items.s: What is the structure of RNA?
items.x: RNA is usually single-stranded - a 'single helix' in exam language - while DNA is a double helix.

items.s: Which one of the following Union Ministries implements the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.x: In India the Ministry of Environment and Forests (now MoEFCC) is the nodal ministry for the Cartagena Protocol; GEAC under it approves GM organisms.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: The weight of a brain of a normal human adult is about
items.x: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3-1.4 kg, i.e. about 3 pounds.

items.s: Why is the ‘Caps Lock’ key referred to as a toggle key?
o: Because it cannot be used for entering numbers.
Because it cannot be used to delete.
Because it cannot be used to insert.
Because its function goes back and forth every time it is pressed.
items.x: A toggle key switches between two states each time it is pressed; Caps Lock alternates between capital and small letters.

items.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
items.s: Bhakra Nangal Dam is a joint project of
items.x: Bhakra Nangal on the Satluj is a joint venture of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

items.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
items.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
a. Chipko Movement
b. Narmada Bachao Andolan
c. Silent Spring
d. Climate change
List-II:
1. Sundar Lal Bahuguna
2. Al Gore
3. Medha Patkar
4. Rachel Carson
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
items.x: Chipko – Sunderlal Bahuguna, NBA – Medha Patkar, Silent Spring – Rachel Carson, climate change – Al Gore: a-1, b-3, c-4, d-2.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
items.s:
Identify the option that arranges the following initiatives launched by the union government in chronological order of their implementation.

1. Promotion of Rooftop Solar - An initiative to encourage the adoption of rooftop solar panels, aiming to increase renewable energy usage and reduce carbon emissions

2. PM Internship Scheme - A program launched to provide internships to young professionals, enhancing their skills and employability

3. National Green Hydrogen Mission - A mission aimed at promoting the production and use of green hydrogen as a clean energy source
items.x:
If 'rooftop solar' is read as PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024), the order would be 3-1-2, which is not offered; the keyed 1-3-2 follows the 2014 rooftop programme.
Rooftop solar programme (2014) came first, then the National Green Hydrogen Mission (Jan 2023), then the PM Internship Scheme (Oct 2024): 1-3-2.

items.s: Scientists of Texas Institute identified Serotonin receptor gene called HTR7 which makes people
items.x: A variant of the serotonin receptor gene HTR7 was linked to alcoholism (alcohol dependence) in a 2012 study.

items.s:
Which is the correct chronological sequence of the major events given below?

A. SLV-3 Launch

B. Formation of Bangladesh

C. Sikkim becomes 22nd State of the Indian Union

D. Pokharan-I test
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
items.x: Bangladesh was formed in Dec 1971, Pokhran-I came in May 1974, Sikkim became the 22nd state in May 1975, and SLV-3 first flew in Aug 1979 (first success Jul 1980): B-D-C-A.

items.s: India's largest optical Telescope is
items.x: The 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope of ARIES, Nainital (2016) is India's largest optical telescope; the Himalayan Chandra Telescope (Hanle) is 2 m.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Pick up the correct pair among the following.
items.x: In chain surveying a ranging rod is set up to mark the position of stations and to range (align) survey lines; it does not measure distance or angles.

items.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
items.s: Lower power factor of a DG set demands
items.x: A low power factor means more lagging reactive current, so the DG set's alternator needs higher field excitation current.

items.s: ‘Silent Spring’, considered by many as one among the greatest science books of all time, is written by Rachel Carson, the book deals with
items.x: Rachel Carson's Silent Spring (1962) showed how pesticides such as DDT harm wildlife and the environment, so it is about protecting the environment.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Land slides occur mostly in ______ areas.
items.x: Landslides occur mostly in hilly and mountainous areas with steep slopes (Himalayas, Western Ghats).

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: Which element is common to all acids?
items.x: All acids contain hydrogen, which they release as H+ ions in water.

items.s: Which leading IT services company, has launched Topaz, a comprehensive suite of services, solutions, and platforms that harness the power of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies?
items.x: Topaz, the generative-AI suite of services, solutions and platforms, was launched by Infosys in May 2023; Wipro, TCS and HCL are distractors.

items.s: Which one of the following are useful in the detection of landmines
items.x: Honey bees can be trained to detect explosive vapour from landmines through their sense of smell.

items.s: Which one of the following computing is used in the calculations that are carried out simultaneously, operating on the principle that large problems can often be divided into smaller ones, which are then solved concurrently?
items.x: Parallel computing splits a large problem into smaller parts that are solved at the same time on several processors; the 'anti-' and 'socialised' options are not computing terms.

items.s: Which of the following allows Internet access from cellular phones, portable and hand-held computers and other such portable gadgets?
items.x: 'Wireless web' means internet access from cellular phones, hand-held computers and other portable gadgets. Spaceweb, Astroweb and Cosmoweb are not standard terms.

items.s: In which country was the world's first face recognition ATM developed?
items.x: The world's first face-recognition ATM was developed in China (2015, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua Unisplendour).

items.s: 'Eye in the sky' is the name given to:
o: AWACS-Airborne Early Warning and Control System
items.x: AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) aircraft are called the "eye in the sky" because their rotating radar watches a wide airspace. Sukhoi and MiG are fighters and Agni-III is a missile.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
items.s: Which of the following materials in normally used in a breath analyzer test to ascertain whether a person is drunk or not?
items.x: In the breath analyser, orange acidified potassium dichromate turns green as it oxidises the alcohol in the breath. Permanganate, silica gel and baking soda are not used.

items.s: As per the Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters, CRED 2000 what percentage of deaths in disasters are of women and children?
items.x: Printed key: about 85% of disaster deaths are of women and children (CRED 2000); women and children are the most vulnerable groups.

items.s: Which of the following statements about the 'Amantran' portal launched by Rajnath Singh in January 2023 is INCORRECT?
o: It will be used to extend e-invitations to dignitaries/guests and for the online sale of tickets to the general public for witnessing Republic Day and Independence Day events.
It contains QR code-based authentication for enhanced security.
Passes/tickets will be delivered digitally through emails/sms.
The passes/tickets can be easily cancelled/transferred.
items.x: The Amantran portal (MoD, Jan 2023) sends e-invitations and sells Republic Day/Beating Retreat tickets with QR-code authentication and digital delivery; the 'easily cancelled/transferred' claim is the incorrect one. Moved to e-governance portals.

items.s: Which of the following is not responsible for the increase in the biodiversity of an ecosystem?
items.x: High productivity, intermediate disturbance and greater ecosystem age all raise biodiversity. Fewer trophic levels reduce it, so that is the factor not responsible.

items.s: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
items.x: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas (from wetlands, rice, livestock, gas leaks). Ethane, propane and butane are not counted among the greenhouse gases.

items.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
items.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
a. Mycology
b. Palynology
c. Oncology
d. Paleontology
List-II: i. study of pollen grains ii. study of treatment of tumours iii. study of fossils of animals and plants iv. study of fungi
items.x: Mycology is the study of fungi, palynology of pollen, oncology of tumours and palaeontology of fossils, so (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
items.s: Which is the dirtiest city in India according to Swachh Surveksham 2017?
items.x: In Swachh Survekshan 2017 (results of 4 May 2017) Gonda in Uttar Pradesh was ranked the dirtiest city, while Indore was the cleanest.

items.s: Which among the following ballistic missiles was tested successfully by India in December 2016?
items.x: Agni-V was test-fired on 26 December 2016 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam (Wheeler) Island, its fourth test and first canister test from a full mobile launcher. Agni-IV was tested on 2 January 2017.

items.s: Among the following statements, which one is correct regarding F-18 Super Hornet?
o: It is a fighterjet, developed by US aerospace company.
It can be used both in day and night.
It is being used by air force of 8 countries.
items.x:
Printed key: (c) used by 8 countries' air forces (true of the Hornet family). Strictly, (a) US-developed fighter and (b) day-and-night capable are also true of the Super Hornet (general knowledge, not checked).
Option c is the printed key: the F/A-18 Hornet family flies with about eight air forces (USA, Canada, Australia, Spain, Kuwait, Finland, Switzerland, Malaysia). Statements a and b are also broadly true of the Super Hornet, so the stem is loose.

items.s: Which algae is used in control of Malaria?
items.x:
Printed key: all of these. Strictly: only Chara/Nitella are the textbook mosquito-control algae; Cladophora has no source and Chlorella only lab larvicidal studies (PeerJ 2023).
Some algae release substances toxic to mosquito larvae; textbooks name Chara and Nitella, and Chlorella extracts are larvicidal in lab studies. The printed key 'All of these' is kept but not verified.

items.s: When you start typing the same value as of some cells on same column, Excel automatically shows that text. This feature is known as :
items.x: AutoComplete in Excel suggests the rest of an entry when you start typing text already present in that column. AutoFill extends series, AutoCorrect fixes typos.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Name the Soviet Union suborbital flight carrying two dogs Dezik and Tsygan.
items.at: An R-1V rocket flight of 22 July 1951 (first animals recovered alive from a suborbital flight)
items.x: Dezik and Tsygan flew on a Soviet R-1 (R-1V) suborbital rocket on 22 July 1951 and were recovered alive. The printed answer 'Robotics spacecraft' names no flight.

items.src: Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidhana Pa
items.s: As per UNISDR statistics, approximately how much percentage of disasters in the world are caused by epidemics?
items.x: Printed key kept: UNISDR data put epidemics at about 15% of disasters worldwide.

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Which of the following metal is the best conductor of electricity?
items.x: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, ahead of copper and aluminium. Off-topic (physics).

items.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
items.s: Name the e-Governance initiative launched in the year 2024 to accelerate e-Governance services in India
items.x: GI Cloud 'MeghRaj' was launched by MeitY to accelerate delivery of e-services while optimising ICT spending. It was launched in February 2014, so '2024' in the stem is a misprint; MyGov (2014) is citizen engagement, ARPANET is the US forerunner of the internet and Digital India came in 2015.

items.s:
Regarding Rafale Jet fighters which of the following is incorrect

a. An agreement was signed between heads of Indo-France Governments in September 2016

b. As per the agreement of September 2016 India has to buy 126 jet fighters

c. France company made a partnership with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited

d. Manufacturer of Rafale aircraft is Dassault Aviation
items.x: The Sep 2016 deal was for 36 Rafales, not 126 (b is wrong), and Dassault's offset partner was Reliance, not HAL (c is wrong). Dassault Aviation is the maker (d is true).

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: From environmental considerations, which of the following is a better option to serve Tea or trains?
o: Serving in glass cups or metal glasses, which are reusable
items.x: Reusable glass or metal cups create no waste. Paper cups are plastic-lined, plastic glasses are single-use, and kulhads, though biodegradable, use topsoil and kiln fuel each time.

items.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of India's advanced satellite INSAT-4A:

A. INSAT-4A was launched in December, 2005 from New Mexico.

B. The European commercial launch service provider Ariane space was associated with the launch of INSAT-4A.

C. Tata-Sky-a digital cable service provider is associated with DTH television broadcasting services from INSAT-4A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
items.x: INSAT-4A was launched in December 2005 from Kourou, French Guiana (not New Mexico) on an Arianespace Ariane-5 (B), and Tata Sky's DTH service uses it (C). So B and C.

items.s: Data scientists require the following skills.
items.x: Data scientists need statistics, machine learning and data visualisation together, so 'all of the above'.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a computer virus?
items.x: Webroot is an antivirus product; rootkits, trojans and bots are malware.

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
items.x: Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

items.s: The term LIDAR stands for?
o: Low Income and Drought Affected Regions
Licensed Development Agency of the Region
items.x: LIDAR = Light Detection and Ranging: a remote-sensing method that uses laser pulses to measure distances and make 3-D maps.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: Which of the following is not a correct statement?
o: 120 Crore persons enrolled under AADHAAR till june, 2017
AADHAAR is a 12 digit unique number
It is mandatory now to link cell phone number of individuals with AADHAAR
At present there is no policy to take back if a person wants to give up AADHAAR
items.x:
mobile-Aadhaar linking was mandatory in 2017 — now not mandatory: the Supreme Court (Puttaswamy, Sept 2018) struck down the DoT circular (general knowledge)
About 116 crore were enrolled by June 2017 (120 crore was crossed only in 2018), so statement 1 was wrong; Aadhaar is 12-digit, mobile-Aadhaar linking was then mandated and there was no opt-out policy.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s: What is the name of an AI-first set of services, solutions, and platforms launched by Infosys to help amplify the potential of humans, enterprises and communities to tap into the next generation of opportunities to create value from unprecedented innovations, connected ecosystems and pervasive efficiencies?
items.x: Infosys launched Topaz (May 2023), an AI-first set of services, solutions and platforms built on generative AI.

items.s: A religious fair is going to happen in Vijayawada. As a Police Officer you have been asked to organise a stampede-free religious fair. You will ―
o: Issue a warning to the public and hope for the best
Limit the number of visitors strictly
Make proper arrangements to control the crowd by deploying police officers at various places
Cancel the fair if crowd management seems difficult
items.x: Proper crowd control through police deployment at key places manages the crowd while keeping the fair open; warning only, strict limits or cancelling are not the answer.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
items.x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

items.s: Recently, a species of tailless rabbits looking like rats were found in the state of
items.x: The tailless, rat-like rabbit relative in the news (a pika, Ochotona) was reported from Sikkim.

items.s: ____ is a collaboration between five federal agencies that are major users and producers of satellite land remote sensing data.
items.x: JACIE (Joint Agency Commercial Imagery Evaluation) is a collaboration of US agencies (NASA, NOAA, NGA, USGS, USDA) that use and produce satellite land remote-sensing data; the other options are Indian institutes.

items.s: India's INS Virat represented India in the International Fleet Review during 15-20 February, 2001. Britain was represented by
items.x: At India's first International Fleet Review (Mumbai, February 2001) the Royal Navy was represented by the frigate HMS Cumberland. HMAS Darwin is Australian, HMS Hermes had become India's INS Viraat, and there is no 'HMS Random'.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: The reaction of sodium Hydroxide with Hydrochloric acid leading to formation of salt and water is a?
items.x: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is a neutralisation, a double displacement reaction (ions exchange partners).

items.s: Which of the following best describes a private, company wide network, closed to public access?
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Intranet); it is added as option 6.
A private, company-wide network closed to public access is an intranet. The printed options repeat 'Internet' (option b is evidently a misprint of 'Intranet'); a VPN is a secure tunnel over a public network, cloud computing is remote services, and an extranet opens part of the network to outsiders.

items.s: Which one of the following is the best example of desiccant?
items.x: Silica gel absorbs moisture and is the standard desiccant (in packets with shoes, medicines, electronics). Polystyrene is a plastic, and NaCl and Na2CO3 are not used as desiccants.

items.s: Which of the following would be the smallest and fastest computer imitating brain working –
items.x: The book key is the quantum computer, the smallest and fastest computing approach (qubits, entanglement in silicon).

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Identify the correct sequence of the following on the basis of establishment year
items.x: Founding years: LinkedIn 2002 (launched 2003), Facebook 2004, YouTube 2005, Twitter 2006.

items.s: Which of the following companies has launched Topaz, an AI-first set of services, solutions, and platforms using generative artificial intelligence technologies?
items.x: Topaz, an AI-first set of services, solutions and platforms using generative AI, was launched by Infosys (May 2023); Accenture, Wipro and IBM are distractors.

items.s: Recently, there was a growing awareness in our country about the importance of Himalayan nettle (Girardinia diversifolia) because it is found to be a sustainable source of
items.x: Himalayan nettle (Girardinia diversifolia) is a sustainable source of strong textile fibre (UPSC 2019 key d).

items.s: Which one of the following cities was ranked the dirtiest by the Urban Development Ministry in a list released in May, 2017?
items.x: In Swachh Survekshan 2017 (results of 4 May 2017) Gonda in Uttar Pradesh was ranked the dirtiest city, while Indore was the cleanest.

items.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
items.s: An iron nail dipped into Copper sulphate solution turns into the following colour?
items.x: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate; the nail gets a reddish-brown copper coating (solution turns pale green).

items.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
items.s: Which of the following is nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agent
items.x: Meloxicam is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) – the vulture-safe substitute for diclofenac; prednisolone, betamethasone and hydrocortisone are corticosteroids.

items.s: What is the CAM in computer graphics?
o: Use of a computer to assist in all operations of a manufacturing plant.
Use of a computer to assist in the capturing image and uploading in the social networks.
Use of a computer to assist camcord to improve the image quality.
None of the statements ‘a’, ‘b’ and ‘c’ given above is correct description of CAM.
items.x: CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) is the use of computers to plan, run and control the operations of a manufacturing plant; it is often paired with CAD.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: Name the homologous series with an -OH functional group.
items.x: Alcohols form the homologous series with the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group. Hydroxide is the OH- ion of bases, not a functional group.

items.s: ITIR stands for
items.x: ITIR = Information Technology Investment Region: the 2008 policy resolution (Ministry of Communications and IT) for large delineated regions (about 40 sq km) for IT, ITES and electronic hardware units, e.g. Bengaluru, Hyderabad. It is not 'International' or 'Industrial'.

items.s: HIB vaccine was prepared by Serum Institute of India. Where is it located?
items.x: Serum Institute of India is based in Pune.

items.s: On December 11 India tested indigenously designed SANT missile at
items.x: DRDO and the IAF flight-tested the helicopter-launched SANT (stand-off anti-tank) missile from the Pokhran ranges, Rajasthan, on 11 December 2021. Balasore/Chandipur and Thiruvananthapuram were not the site.
